material_facts.fact: The petitioners operated hostels or paying-guest accommodation for working men, working women and similar occupants.
The inmates shared rooms primarily because independent houses, flats or apartments were less affordable.
The inmates used the hostel premises after work for sleeping, eating, bathing, washing clothes and other ordinary residential activities.
The hostel facilities included sleeping rooms, bathrooms, toilets, washing areas, common kitchens and dining or refreshment areas.
The petitioners received rent and operated the hostels as businesses.
Municipal, water and related authorities classified or reclassified the hostel properties under commercial tariffs.
Commercial classification resulted in enhanced demands for property tax, water tax, water charges and, in some cases, electricity charges.
The economic burden of higher tariffs would ultimately be passed on to hostel inmates.
The authorities relied on the business nature of hostel operations and provisions referring to private hostels or lodging houses.
The petitioners relied on statutory definitions treating use of a house or part of it as a sleeping apartment as residence.
The respondents did not produce documentary evidence establishing that prior notice or communication had been given before tariff conversion.
A statutory appeal was available under Section 100 of the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Act, 1998.
The petitioners approached the High Court directly under Article 226 instead of first pursuing the statutory appeal.
An earlier Madras High Court GST judgment dated 22 March 2024 had treated comparable hostel use from the recipient's perspective as residential use.

undisputed_facts: The occupants used rooms for sleeping and ordinary daily living.
The authorities imposed or sought to impose commercial tariffs.
Higher taxes and charges could be passed on to inmates.

disputed_facts_or_characterisations.question: Whether the physical and functional use of the hostel premises was residential or commercial.
disputed_facts_or_characterisations.petitioners_position: The recipients used the premises only as residences or sleeping apartments.
disputed_facts_or_characterisations.respondents_position: The hostel business and regulatory classification justified commercial treatment.

disputed_facts_or_characterisations.question: Whether adequate prior notice was issued before reclassification.
disputed_facts_or_characterisations.petitioners_position: No prior notice or opportunity was given.
disputed_facts_or_characterisations.respondents_position: The judgment records no documentary proof produced by the respondents establishing prior communication.

facts_not_established_from_the_order: The exact date on which each petitioner began hostel operations.
The exact filing date of every writ petition.
The exact occupancy, rent and financial profile of every hostel.
Whether every room in every hostel was inspected before assessment.
Whether any individual room was used for a separate commercial activity.

fact_interpretation_boundary.rule: This artifact records factual propositions and party positions only. Legal conclusions and judicial interpretations belong in later artifacts.
